Based on my research, here is what I found regarding the Ambetter of Tennessee denial for CPT 28296 (bunion/hallux valgus surgery):

```json
{
  "policy_found": false,
  "policy_title": null,
  "policy_number": null,
  "policy_url": null,
  "effective_date": null,
  "criteria_quotes": [],
  "appeal_deadline": "2027-02-06 (180 days from the 2026-08-10 notice date, per Ambetter of Tennessee's own appeal form, which states: \"This form must be filed within 180 days of an adverse determination.\")",
  "submission_route": "Mail or fax a written appeal (or the plan's Grievance, Appeal, Concern or Recommendation Form) to: Ambetter of Tennessee, Attn: Grievances and Appeals Department, 12515-8 Research Blvd Ste 400, Austin, TX 78759. Phone: 1-833-709-4735 (Relay 711). Fax: 1-833-886-7956 (Grievances & Appeals). Include the reference/tracking number from the denial letter (here, POC-C1EE0F5DA7-11270) and any supporting clinical documentation. A member may also authorize a representative (e.g., the treating podiatrist/surgeon) to file on their behalf using Ambetter's Authorized Representative Designation Form.",
  "how_to_obtain_criteria": "I checked Ambetter of Tennessee's published 'Clinical & Payment Policies' list (the Ambetter of Tennessee Clinical Policy Manual, hosted at ambetterhealth.com/en/tn/provider-resources/clinical-payment-policies/). It contains dozens of named CP.MP-numbered medical policies (e.g., Bariatric Surgery CP.MP.37, Panniculectomy CP.MP.109, Cosmetic and Reconstructive Procedures CP.MP.31), but there is no listed policy for bunionectomy, hallux valgus, or general 'foot surgery.' Critically, the same page states in its own governing language: 'Ambetter of Tennessee utilizes InterQual\u00ae criteria for those medical technologies, procedures or pharmaceutical treatments for which an Ambetter of Tennessee clinical policy does not exist... You may access the InterQual\u00ae SmartSheet(s)\u2122 ... by logging into the secure provider portal or by calling Ambetter of Tennessee.' Because CPT 28296 / hallux valgus correction is not one of the enumerated CP.MP policies, the applicable medical-necessity criteria are almost certainly the proprietary InterQual\u00ae 'Exostectomy, First Metatarsophalangeal (MTP) Joint (Bunionectomy)' criteria set (this is the InterQual category other Centene/insurer foot-surgery policies point to). InterQual criteria are a licensed, copyrighted clinical decision-support product (owned by Change Healthcare/Optum) and are NOT published publicly online \u2014 they exist only inside the provider portal or by phone request. Therefore, to get the exact criteria applied to Sawyer's case, the patient or their surgeon's office should: (1) call Ambetter of Tennessee Member/Provider Services at 1-833-709-4735 and specifically request 'the InterQual SmartSheet criteria used to deny prior authorization reference POC-C1EE0F5DA7-11270 for CPT 28296'; (2) request the full case file/clinical rationale that the medical director used, which the plan is required to provide upon appeal request under ACA/ERISA-type disclosure rules; and (3) have the treating provider log into the Ambetter secure provider portal, where InterQual SmartSheets for the relevant procedure category can be viewed. The plan is generally obligated to disclose the specific criteria relied upon in a denial when an appeal is filed.",
  "confidence": "medium",
  "notes": "The denial letter itself gives no policy name/number \u2014 it only says the request was denied for 'incomplete documentation' that 'does not allow a determination of medical necessity,' without citing a specific medical policy. I confirmed via Ambetter of Tennessee's official clinical policy manual page that (a) they maintain a public list of plan-specific CP.MP-numbered policies, (b) bunionectomy/hallux valgus is not among them, and (c) for any procedure not covered by a plan-specific policy, they explicitly default to proprietary InterQual\u00ae criteria that are not publicly posted. I could not verify a Tennessee-specific 'Surgery of the Foot' or 'Bunionectomy' CP.MP policy exists at all for Ambetter/Centene \u2014 other payers (Aetna, UnitedHealthcare, Cigna) do have public bunionectomy policies, but those are NOT the governing document for this Ambetter of Tennessee plan and should not be cited to Ambetter in an appeal. The 180-day appeal deadline and mailing/fax address were confirmed directly from Ambetter of Tennessee's own member Grievance/Appeal form (AMB18-TN-C-00245), which matches the deadline stated in the denial notice. Recommendation for the appeal: rather than arguing against specific published criteria (none are public), the strongest approach is to (1) request the InterQual criteria/case rationale in writing before or with the appeal, and (2) submit complete supporting documentation addressing the typical elements InterQual/other payers use for bunionectomy medical necessity \u2014 e.g., symptomatic hallux valgus with pain interfering with function, radiographic hallux valgus angle measurements, failure of a defined trial of conservative treatment (wide/accommodative shoewear, orthotics, padding, NSAIDs, activity modification), and absence of purely cosmetic indication \u2014 since the stated denial reason was 'incomplete documentation,' not a substantive medical-necessity failure."
}
```

**Bottom line:** I could not find a publicly available, Ambetter/Centene-specific medical policy document containing medical-necessity criteria for CPT 28296 (bunionectomy/hallux valgus correction). Ambetter of Tennessee's own clinical policy manual list does not include a bunion/hallux valgus/foot surgery policy, and the manual states that when no plan-specific policy exists, it defaults to proprietary InterQual® criteria accessible only via the secure provider portal or by phone — not published online. The patient's best path is to explicitly request (in writing, referencing tracking number POC-C1EE0F5DA7-11270) the specific InterQual criteria and case rationale used, and to submit the appeal with complete clinical documentation (exam findings, x-ray measurements, conservative treatment history) to Ambetter of Tennessee's Grievances and Appeals Department by the 2027-02-06 deadline.
